title: Rwanda's Services Bet: Kigali's Finance Hub, $94.7m in Meetings, 10 Stocks | The Six, Ep. 21
lede: Services made up 52% of Rwanda's economy in 2025, but finance is still under 3% of GDP. Kigali is trying to change that with a financial centre offering 3% corporate tax, a growing conference trade and a stock exchange worth about $4.6 billion. On the latest global ranking, Kigali is third in Africa but has slipped to 80th.
keyPoints: Rwanda's economy grew 9.4% in 2025; services were 52% of GDP and grew 9% (NISR; Ministry of Finance).
The Kigali International Financial Centre, set up in 2020, reports more than $1 billion in targeted investment commitments and over 300 investors (The New Times; TechCabal).
On the Global Financial Centres Index of September 2026, Kigali ranked 80th of 117 and third in Africa, after Casablanca and Mauritius; it was 65th a year earlier (Z/Yen GFCI 38 and 40).
The Rwanda Stock Exchange had a market value of about Rwf6.6 trillion (about $4.6 billion) in February 2026 across shares and bonds, with 10 equity listings (Rwanda Stock Exchange).
Meetings and events earned Rwanda $94.7 million in 2025, up from $85 million in 2024; the target is $224 million (Rwanda Development Board via The New Times).
